ended: Lost the West 1st Round 1-4 to SA

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (frontcourt-built)
archetype.definition: Portland climbed from a losing start into its first playoff win since 2020-21 on the strength of its bigs and the offensive glass, then was outclassed by San Antonio in five games.

report.headline: A frontcourt-built return to the playoffs, capped by the league's worst turnover rate

recap.finish: 42-40, fourth in the Northwest; lost the West 1st Round 1-4 to SA
recap.body:
This was a .500 team in every sense that matters, and an honest one. Its Net Rtg of -0.3 ranked 19th, its offense ranked 20th and its defense 14th, and the margin implied 40 wins against the 42 it got. Two wins of close-game luck is little. Against a franchise that won 36 games a year ago and 21 the year before, the climb is real, and it came from a clear identity: crash the offensive glass, fire threes at volume, and lean on a deep group of centers.

The season started badly before it started well. A 4-2 October gave way to a 4-10 November in which Portland allowed 123.07 points a game, and the record sat at 14-20 after December. From January on the defense steadied. A 9-6 month pulled them to 23-26, February broke even, and a 10-6 March, allowing just 108 a game, pushed them over .500 for the first time since the opening weeks. They closed 7-3 over the last 10 with a differential of 13.1 a game. That run should be read with some care: Brooklyn, Milwaukee, Washington, New Orleans and Sacramento made up much of it, and the two real tests, at Denver in overtime and at San Antonio, were both losses.

The engine was the frontcourt, graded B+ against C- marks for both the backcourt and the wings. Donovan Clingan led the team in Win Shares at 8.6 with 892 rebounds, ranked eighth on the center tab. Robert Williams gave them a 72.2 TS % and a 4.5 BPM in about a thousand minutes. Toumani Camara played all 82 games and made 219 threes. Together they drove an ORB % of 31.3, second in the league, which gave a mediocre shooting team extra chances. Deni Avdija was the one perimeter player who drove winning: an All-Star season with 1,598 points, 442 assists, a 60.0 TS % and 7.0 Win Shares, sixth on the small forward tab.

The ceiling was set by the ball and the arc. Portland took threes at the league's third-highest rate but hit only 34.3 %, 27th, and its 14.6 TOV % was the worst in the league. That combination left the offense below average despite the second-chance points. In the backcourt, Shaedon Sharpe used 30.5 % of possessions at a 54.6 TS % with a -1.4 BPM, and Caleb Love's 49.7 TS % came with a -7.9 On-Off. Jrue Holiday's +9.8 On-Off was the only guard number that pointed up, and he played 53 games.

The San Antonio series exposed all of it. Portland stole Game 2 on the road, 106-103, then lost the next three by double digits. Its 50.8 TS % was the worst of the 16 playoff teams, and the Spurs shot 41.8 % from three, also the worst mark allowed. Clingan's shooting fell apart (36.6 TS %, -17.9 On-Off) while Williams was the best player on the floor for Portland, with a 10.8 BPM and a +26.6 On-Off. Sharpe, listed out, managed only 67 minutes. Oddly, the Blazers protected the ball well in the series (11.5 TOV %, third), so this loss was about shot-making on both ends.

highlights.title: Bigs and the offensive glass
highlights.body: The frontcourt graded B+, the one strong group on the roster, and combined for 21.4 Win Shares. Clingan and Williams both rank among the top dozen centers on the site, and their work produced a 31.3 ORB %, second in the league and up from 29.2 last season. It is built on young, productive bigs and has trended up two straight years, so it looks durable.

highlights.title: Avdija's All-Star season
highlights.body: Avdija carried the perimeter by himself: 1,598 points and 442 assists at a 60.0 TS % on 29.3 % usage, with a 4.3 BPM. That high usage and that efficiency came together, which no Portland guard managed. He ranks sixth among small forwards, so this is a top-tier creator the team can build around.

highlights.title: The defense grew up after November
highlights.body: After allowing 123.07 a game in November, Portland allowed 111.73 in January and 108 in March. That carried the defense to a 114.7 DRtg, 14th in the league. The full-season mark matches last year's, so the middle-of-the-pack defense looks like the team's level rather than a fluke. The late surge came partly against weak opponents.

lowlights.title: Turnovers and misses from three
lowlights.body: A 46.9 % 3PA Rate paired with a 34.3 3P % meant the volume rarely paid off. A league-worst 14.6 TOV % also gave away possessions the offensive rebounding had won back. Both problems carried over from last season's 34.2 % and 13.8 TOV %, and the turnovers got worse, so this is a roster trait, not variance.

lowlights.title: Guards who couldn't drive winning
lowlights.body: The backcourt graded C-. Sharpe used the most possessions on the team at a below-average 54.6 TS %, and Love posted a 49.7 TS % with a -7.9 On-Off. The wings behind Avdija were thin too: Sidy Cissoko played 1,435 minutes with a -4.0 BPM, ranked 93rd of 96 small forwards. Holiday's +9.8 On-Off shows what steady guard play is worth here.

lowlights.title: Shooting collapse against San Antonio
lowlights.body: In the playoffs Portland scored 100 a game with a 50.8 TS %, last among playoff teams. It also allowed the Spurs to hit 41.8 % from three. The lone win came in Game 2, and the last three games were not close. Five games is a small sample, but the shot-making gap matched the regular season's weakness.

arc.note: A 4-10 November left them 14-20 at the turn of the year, then a winning January and a 10-6 March lifted them above .500. They finished 7-3 over the last 10 before a five-game exit.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is clear: Clingan, Williams and Camara in a B+ frontcourt, plus Avdija on the wing, accounted for most of the value. The 42 wins are close to what the margin earned (40), so there is little luck to give back. There is also little cushion: a -0.3 Net Rtg is a play-in-level team that happened to get in. The work is on the perimeter. Both the backcourt and the wings graded C-, the league-worst turnover rate and 27th-ranked 3P % are long-running problems, and Sharpe's heavy usage has not yet turned into efficient scoring. Williams' production in limited minutes, regular season and playoffs alike, argues for a bigger role. Do not read too much into the late 13.1-a-game surge, since it came largely against weak opponents.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus a five-game series; playoff splits are a small sample.
